title: Lazur vs Wispr Flow on Mac: AI dictation or a voice assistant that sees your screen
metaTitle: Lazur vs Wispr Flow: which one fits your Mac
description: Lazur vs Wispr Flow on Mac: Wispr Flow is dictation on Mac, Windows and phones. Lazur is a Mac voice assistant that sees your screen and dictates too.
intro: Lazur vs Wispr Flow comes down to one question. Do you want dictation only, or dictation plus an assistant that sees your screen? Wispr Flow is the better pick for dictation alone, especially if you also need Windows or a phone. Lazur is the better pick if you want answers and pointing help on your Mac, with dictation included.
tldr: Wispr Flow is an AI dictation app. Lazur is a voice assistant that also dictates.
Pick Wispr Flow if dictation is the whole job, or you need Windows or a phone too.
Pick Lazur if you want answers about your screen, pointing help and dictation in one Mac app.
Wispr Flow lists a free plan and Pro at $15/user/mo monthly or $12/user/mo billed annually. Lazur has a 3-day Pro trial, then Pro at $18/month.

verdict: Pick Wispr Flow if dictation is the whole job, you need Windows or a phone, or you dictate in many languages. Pick Lazur if you use a Mac every day and want help with what is on your screen as well as dictation. If you only want clean text in email and documents, Wispr Flow is the simpler choice.

blocks.text: What each app does on your Mac

Wispr Flow is a dictation app. You hold a key, talk, and it types clean text wherever your cursor sits. Lazur is a voice assistant that also dictates. You hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and it answers out loud. You hold fn to dictate.

That split matters more than any feature list. Say you are writing a reply to a vendor email. Dictation is the fast part, and both apps handle it. Now say you cannot find the setting that turns off a sync option. Dictation cannot help with that. Lazur can look at the screen and draw a circle around the control.

Most of your day is not dictation. You switch between mail, a spreadsheet, a PDF and a browser. Each switch is a chance to get stuck. That is where a screen-aware assistant earns its place. Dictation alone never sees the PDF you are reading.
Dictation head to head: which one types cleaner text

Wispr Flow puts most of its effort into dictation. Its homepage says it removes filler words, catches mid-sentence corrections and learns custom names and terms. It also offers snippets and per-app tone settings. One independent review from August 2026, which contains affiliate links, says the writer produces text much faster with it and that the cleanup handles rambling speech well.

The same review has limits. The writer still rereads important text, because cleanup sometimes changes the shape of a sentence. Proper nouns and unusual phrases trip it up, and noisy rooms cause errors. The writer also felt odd talking to a laptop in an open office. Treat that as one person's view. The review ran no speed or accuracy benchmarks.

Lazur dictates too. Hold fn, speak, and formatted text appears at the cursor in any app. You also get snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots. Lazur's site does not list a filler-word cleanup feature or a language count. Test it on your own writing before you decide.

How much does voice save? A lab study is the closest thing to a number. Ruan and colleagues found English speech input was 2.93 times faster than a keyboard for short messages on touchscreen phones. Speech ran at 153 words per minute, and the keyboard at 52. That study used phones, not Macs, and it did not test Wispr Flow. Use it as a rough guide, not a promise.

Short sentences are easy in either app. Long paragraphs with names, prices and dates need a read-through. Check every number before you send. A quick proofread costs less time than an email with a wrong figure.
A one-week test you can run on your own text

items: Day 1: dictate three emails in your normal style with each app. Time how long the fixes take.
Day 2: dictate a sentence with a name, a product and a term the app might not know. Note every error.
Day 3: repeat a task in a noisy room or an open office. Check whether you still trust the output.
Day 4: ask Lazur about a settings panel you cannot read. See whether the circle and label help.
Day 5: compare your totals. Decide which errors you can live with, and which app you would open first.

blocks.text: Where Lazur goes beyond typing

Lazur sees your screen only while you hold ⌥ ⌘. Ask where something is, and it draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. It does not click for you. You stay in control of the mouse and the keyboard.

Say a settings panel has a toggle you cannot find. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where it is. Lazur circles the control and labels it. You click it yourself. If you need more steps, ask Lazur to walk you through it, and it will pause after each one.

Everyday requests work by voice too. Lazur handles timers, Apple Reminders, Calendar events, notes, music and volume, opening apps and links, web search and Shortcuts. Longer research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report.
Pricing: what each site charges

Wispr Flow lists a free plan at $0/mo with limited words per week. Pro is $15/user/mo billed monthly, or $12/user/mo billed annually. Pro removes the dictation word limit and adds a shared team workspace. Growth and Enterprise are listed too, but the Growth page shows two sets of prices. Check the pricing page before you buy.

The free plan does not publish a word count. Its help article says the allowance differs by platform and by account. When you hit the cap, new dictations stop until the window resets or you upgrade. Unused words do not carry over. Check your own limit in the app before you rely on it.

Lazur has a 3-day Pro trial with no credit card. The trial starts when you first open the app, not when you pay. Pro is $18/month, or $15/month billed annually, with 150 AI actions. Power is $120/month, or $96/month billed annually, with 1,000 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both plans.

blocks.title: Compare the right tiers
blocks.text: Compare Wispr Flow Pro with Lazur Pro, not a free plan with a trial. Dictation is unlimited on both Lazur plans. Lazur's AI actions are a separate limit, so check how many you use in a normal week.
Privacy: what leaves your Mac

Wispr Flow sends your speech to the cloud for transcription. Its privacy page says transcription always happens in the cloud. Audio is captured only after you press the shortcut. It is deleted once transcribed, unless you turn on Dictation cloud storage. Stored data uses AES-256 on secure cloud servers.

You control more of Wispr's data than you might expect. Local history can be kept, auto-deleted after 24 hours, or never saved. Set it in Settings > Data and Privacy. Model training is a separate switch. Turning it off means audio, transcripts and edits are not used for training. The homepage also lists SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and HIPAA compliance. Those are company claims, so verify them if your work needs them.

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. When you ask a question, the audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer. Lazur says they are not stored, and that content is never used to train AI models. Your memory of what you asked and did stays on your Mac. Lazur's site does not describe an offline mode for either feature.

blocks.title: Check retention before client work
blocks.text: If the work involves client data, read the retention setting first. In Wispr Flow, that is Settings > Data and Privacy. Turn off Dictation cloud storage if you do not need it, and turn off model training if your policy requires it.
Who should pick Wispr Flow

items: You want dictation as the main job, on your Mac and on your phone.
You need Windows support, because Lazur runs only on macOS.
You dictate in many languages and want 100+ language support.
You want meeting notes with named speakers, on Mac or Windows.

blocks.text: Who should pick Lazur

items: You get stuck in apps and want a voice that points at the right control.
You want to ask what something on screen means, and hear the answer.
You want dictation and everyday voice tasks in one Mac app.
You want research to run in the background and return with a report.

blocks.text: Mistakes people make when they compare these two

items: Comparing a free plan with a trial. Wispr's free plan has no published word count, and Lazur's trial is time-limited. Compare the paid tiers first.
Expecting Lazur to do the clicking. Lazur points and guides. You click.
Judging dictation from a demo. Test with your own names, jargon and background noise.
Forgetting the Lazur trial clock. It starts when you first open the app, so open it when you are ready to test.
Skipping the retention setting. Check how long Wispr keeps history before you dictate client notes.

blocks.text: Can you run both apps on one Mac?

Yes, if their shortcuts do not clash. Lazur uses hold fn to dictate and hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask. Check Wispr Flow's shortcut in its settings. If the two overlap, change one. Dictation in one app and questions in the other is a simple split to try.
Your next steps

Start with the question you actually have. If it is about typing speed, run the [speaking vs typing test](/tools/speaking-vs-typing-test) and time yourself. If it is about help inside apps, [download Lazur](/download) and use the trial on one real task. Compare the paid tiers on the [Lazur pricing page](/pricing) before you pay. Read Wispr's privacy page for its retention setting, and check the [Wispr Flow alternatives](/alternatives/wispr-flow) if neither fits.

faq.question: Is Lazur a good Wispr Flow alternative?
faq.answer: If you want more than dictation, yes. Lazur dictates in any Mac app and also answers questions about your screen. It points at buttons and guides you one click at a time. If you only dictate, and you need Windows or a phone, Wispr Flow is the better fit.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur and Wispr Flow together?
faq.answer: Yes, if their shortcuts do not clash. Lazur uses hold fn to dictate and hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask. Check Wispr Flow's shortcut in its settings, and change one of them if the two overlap.

faq.question: Is Wispr Flow cheaper than Lazur?
faq.answer: At the annual rate, Wispr Flow Pro is $12/user/mo billed annually. Lazur Pro is $15/month billed annually. Monthly, Wispr Pro is $15/user/mo and Lazur Pro is $18/month. Lazur also includes the screen-aware assistant, so the two are not the same product.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: No. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available yet.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur draws a circle and a label around what you need, or guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click. It does not operate other apps for you.

faq.question: Is my audio stored?
faq.answer: Wispr Flow deletes audio after transcription, unless Dictation cloud storage is on. Lazur says the audio and screenshots it sends to AI providers are not stored, and that content is never used to train AI models. Read both privacy pages before you use either with client work.
